key_insight: Evaluator bias in multi-agent LLM systems can spread from one agent to others like contagion, even when all agents use the same underlying model.
engineering_relevance: Designing evaluator committees and bias-aware agent networks can materially reduce error propagation, with a 3-member committee cutting effective contagion by 72.4%.
method: Defined Contagion Networks to measure how evaluator bias propagates across interacting LLM agents.
Ran a controlled 3-agent experiment with DeepSeek-chat under three evaluator bias profiles: structured, balanced, and evidence-based.
Computed the Cross-Agent Contagion Matrix (Gamma_3) and analyzed propagation regimes via the spectral radius rho(Gamma_N).
evidence_signal: In the 3-agent study, contagion coefficients remained nonzero at gamma = 0.157 to 0.352, while increasing committee size from k=1 to k=3 reduced effective contagion by 72.4%.
watch_item: Results come from a controlled setup on one model family, so real-world multi-model systems may show different propagation strength and dynamics.
paper_title: Contagion Networks: Evaluator Bias Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
